title: PHREEQC thermal fixed-point failure after hydroxide-suspension filtration
original_physical_forecast: The suspension can replenish dissolved hydroxide by consuming solid Mg(OH)2. Its filtrate lacks that reserve and should acidify much more under the same acid dose.

event.detail: phreeqc-aqueous could not solve this state: coupled aqueous temperature did not converge within 64 passes (last residual 3.402842e-3 K)

generic_limit: An exit0 is not accepted chemistry. No new runtime, parameter change or calibration is assigned.
observed: Filtering transfers aqueous Mg+2, water and analytical base into v3 while retaining solid Mg(OH)2 in v2. The target solve reaches 64 passes with residual 0.003402842 K and declines. The initial filtrate pH measurement emits ph-meter-has-no-solution; later HCl obtains pH 2.04993. Suspension pH changes from 10.39568 to 9.67121. The original capacity forecast remains unclosed.
rollback_scope: Filtering itself remains committed. The failing aqueous trial does not visibly replace the transferred inventory. Combined pre/post H/O/Mg/charge residuals are zero and all vessel temperatures/excess-enthalpy fields are unchanged. Equal temperatures alone are not a complete energy-balance proof.
acceptance_lanes: Diagnose exact postfilter aqueous thermal fixed point with owned basis/water/energy and source reference; preserve64pass failure.

Keep genuine nonconvergence honest and withhold stale pH. Verify successful physically supported readback or named unsupported scope; do not loosen tolerance/increase passes without convergence evidence.
Compare solids-containing suspension and finite filtrate, next acid dose, varied ordering, rollback of failed solver trial and native/Wasm parity.
